Here are the most important follow-up items I spotted while re‑scanning the project:

- **NotificationManager.swift:133-175** – `lastScheduledMilestone` only ever increases. When the user resets progress (`RelapsedView`), we never reset this flag or clear any previously scheduled milestone notifications, so `scheduleMilestoneNotifications()` will skip all upcoming milestones for the new quit date. We should reset `lastScheduledMilestone` (and optionally cancel existing `milestone-*` requests) whenever the counter is reset.

- **RelapsedView.swift:185-203** – Although the reset button now clears the streak/date storage, it doesn’t touch notification state (milestone reminders, motivational quote index, etc.). Without clearing those, users can still receive celebratory notifications that refer to the pre-reset streak. Consider invoking a `NotificationManager` reset (remove pending milestone notifications, reset `lastScheduledMilestone`, reschedule daily check-ins).

- **DailyCheckInView.swift:19-24 & 291-301** – Limiting `checkInDates` to the newest 365 entries also caps `totalCheckInDays` at 365, so the “Total Days” card (and any achievements keyed off it) will never show values beyond a year. We need a separate lifetime counter that isn’t trimmed, otherwise long-term users lose their historical totals.

- **ProgressTabView.swift:53-99** – The `longestStreak` fallback now derives from `checkInDatesString`, but since that list is truncated to 365 entries, the computed longest streak can never exceed a year even if the user has been sober longer. Either store the longest streak explicitly (beyond what we already track) or run the calculation over an unbounded dataset.

- **ProfileView.swift:113-135** – “Log Out” simply flips `hasCompletedOnboarding` and refreshes subscription status. All personal data (quit date, streaks, journal entries, saved reasons, notifications) stays in UserDefaults, so the next user sees the previous person’s history. For privacy, the logout flow should either clear sensitive defaults or present a confirmation explaining what remains.

- **HomeView.swift:736-761** – The new `daysCountTask` animation cancels itself only when a new target arrives. If the view disappears (e.g., user switches tabs) while the animation is running, the Task keeps executing because there's no `.onDisappear { daysCountTask?.cancel() }`. That’s minor but can waste work and log warnings in Instruments; it’s worth cancelling when the view leaves the screen.

These are the key issues I’d tackle next to keep the experience and data consistent for users.
